flags: minor: no stated real-world context; item is essentially 'graph and read intersection', which a graphing calculator makes routine
Q031-01.notes: Roots of 2^x - x - 3 = 0: x ~ -2.863 and x ~ 2.4449. Greater root is 2.4 to the nearest tenth. A (-2.9) is the lesser root, a good distractor; D (2.5) catches rounding/estimation errors (2^2.5=5.66>5.5, 2^2.4=5.28<5.4); B (2.0) gives 4 vs 5. Exactly one defensible.

Q031-02.notes: sqrt(x) = x/4 -> x = x^2/16 -> x(x-16)=0 -> a=16 (b=4). Quick by graphing too.

flags: minor: margin at x=9 is narrow (235.79 vs 235), so precise computation is needed; that is fine but rewards a calculator table
Q031-03.notes: f(8)=214.36<220; f(9)=235.79>235; f(10)=259.37>250. At x=0 f=g, so not 'greater'. Smallest positive integer is 9. Choices 7,8,10 are adjacent plausible values; 10 catches those who misjudge the near-tie at 9.

flags: minor: B has a negative slope and is easily eliminated since y clearly increases; D's intercept 6.0 is also quickly eliminated (x=1 gives 7.94 vs 3.1). Effectively a two-way choice between A and C (both give 3.09 at x=1, but diverge at x=4: 6.54 vs 8.91)
Q031-04.notes: Least-squares fit: slope 1.94, intercept 1.15 exactly, so y = 1.94x + 1.15. A swaps slope and intercept.

Q031-05.notes: bx - 3x = 2b + 5 -> x(b-3) = 2b+5 -> x = (2b+5)/(b-3). A sign error on 5; C wrong sign on 3; D sign error in denominator (would require -(2b+5)). Condition b != 3 is correctly stated.
